questions.q: Why are many people opposed to monitoring employee performance?
options: It puts workers under constant pressure.
It is universally deemed anti-human by nature.
It does both mental and physical harm to employees monitored.
It enables firms to squeeze maximal productivity from employees.

questions.q: What is the supporters’ argument for workplace surveillance?
options: It enables employees to refrain from dominating conversations.
It enhances employees’ identification with firms they work in.
It can alert employees to intrusion into their privacy.
It can protect employees against aggressive behavior.

questions.q: What does the author want to show by the example of different numbers of people interacting at lunch tables?
options: Data analysis is key to the successful implementation of workplace surveillance.
Analyzing data gathered from workers can yield something unexpected.
More workmates sitting at a lunch table tend to facilitate interaction and idea sharing.
It is hard to decide on how many people to sit at a lunch table without data analysis.

questions.q: What does much of the positive effect of monitoring initiatives depend on?
options: How frequently employees are to be monitored.
What specific personal information is being excluded.
What steps are taken to minimize their detrimental impact.
How well bosses make known their purpose of monitoring.

questions.q: What concern do monitoring initiatives cause among many staffers?
options: They may empower employers excessively.
They may erode the workplace environment.
They may infringe upon staffers’ entitled freedom.
They may become counterproductive in the long run.
